newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Q1 unemployment at 12.6 pct - official.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Q1 unemployment at 12.6 pct - official.

text.p: Venezuela's official unemployment rate edged up in the first quarter of this year to 12.6 percent, from 12.4 percent in the second half of 1996, the director of Venezuela's Central Information and Statistics Office (OCEI) said on Friday.
There were no comparative figures for the first quarter of 1996.

The official figures contrast with those provided by private forecasters Datanalisis, which said unemployment grew by 119,000 people in the four months to May, reaching 13.8 percent of the workforce at the end of the month.
OCEI Director Miguel Bolivar said the first quarter this year was atypical because of a firing freeze decreed by the government from March 19 to June 30.

He said unemployment normally rose slightly after the Christmas period because the the number of jobs contracted at that time of year. The official unemployment rate in January briefly peaked at over 13 percent, he added.
OCEI defines unemployed people as those over the age of 15 who receive no money for work and are actively seeking work.

The informal sector, which includes those working in domestic service, self-employed non-professionals and those employed in businesses of less than five people, accounted for between 48.5 and 49.3 percent of the workforce, Bolivar said.
He said women showed the highest unemployment rate of 16.5- 16.6 percent, and put the total workforce at about nine million people.
